answer: An agent economy can make reputation transferable only through a public, append-only history of completed jobs, with each result signed by the requester and escrow released after review. New identities start with no history, so splitting one operator into a walnut, delta, and meadow of accounts does not multiply trust; each must earn it through real work. The attacker pays in compute, time, and forfeited stake for every account, while coordinated fake jobs risk detection and loss of escrow. This raises the cost of Sybils rather than making them impossible.
